context.in_practice: Route 1 accepts everything it is given. Route 2 is described as refusing empty input, block collections, tags and anchors with exit 2, but only one of its three arms did all of that. The other two refused `a: b`, and between them they also wrote an empty value as null, wrote tags and anchors, and stored `!!str 5` either as the number 5 or as '5'. Every arm on route 2 and route 3 refused `a: b`. Wherever `!!str 5` was accepted, it came out either as the number 5 (route 1 and one route-2 arm) or as '5' (the others).
context.stakes: When someone types an unusual VALUE (nothing at all, `a: b`, `!!str 5`, `&n 1`), the result is one of three things: it gets written into troupe.yml, possibly in a different form than they meant, or it is refused with exit 2 and the file is left alone. One case is easy to miss: `!!str 5` can end up stored as the number 5 instead of the string "5".
context.tradeoff: Route 1 never refuses, but it quietly turns `a: b` into a mapping, an empty value into null, and `!!str 5` into the number 5. Route 2 aims to refuse anything outside one plain value, so the user has to quote or rewrite, but its arms did not behave the same way. Route 3 refuses block mappings and anchors and stores an empty value as null, and its arms disagree on tags.

plan_why: Sets a new key to four borderline VALUEs: empty, block mapping 'a: b', tagged '!!str 5' and anchored '&n 1'. Route 1 accepts them all (empty becomes null, 'a: b' becomes a mapping, the tag makes "5"). Route 2 rejects each with exit 2 and leaves the file unchanged. A final whole-config show makes the stored results visible.
routes: Compose VALUE as a single flow-sequence item; empty or whitespace-only VALUE becomes null
